gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the AV Access KD-E10 costs $169.99 on AV Access's US store today: that buys the same 100 W laptop charging, dual 4K@60 and HDMI+DP desktop inputs as ChatGPT's $256 TESmert T722 pick, $86.01 less, but on a Mac the two screens mirror instead of extending.
standout_why: Racks & Watts (the cited page) lists four KVMs with no prices; its only laptop-plus-desktop pick is the AV Access iDock C10, which charges at 60 W. The TESmart buying guide (also cited) gives no prices and names only the $699 DisplayLink HDC203-PM24 for Macs. ChatGPT's answer priced three cards but showed no 100 W dock under $256 and did not compare one against another. Neither cited page mentions the KD-E10, and neither notes that the C10 costs $70 more than the KD-E10 while charging at 40 W less.
decides: For a Windows laptop (USB-C with DP Alt Mode and MST) plus a desktop on two monitors, the KD-E10 at $169.99 is the value pick. It beats the T722 ($256), iDock C10 ($239.99, 60 W) and TESmart HDC202-P23 ($419.99, up to 60 W) on price for equal or higher charging power. For a MacBook, the KD-E10 loses because macOS mirrors MST screens. There the T722 at $256 (two USB-C cables) undercuts the iDock M10 at $289.99, and the M10 extends to two screens only on M4/M5 or Pro/Max chips. For one monitor, the TESmart HKS201-P23 at $129.99 needs an HDMI port on the laptop and charges nothing. For a gaming desktop, the $359 HKS202-M24 is HDMI-only and charges nothing, so for a work laptop it is a poor fit. Our page's HDC202-X24 row should drop 'stock unclear': it shows as available today at $699.
